items.name: Orchestral color as the primary compositional parameter
items.description: Rimsky-Korsakov thought in colors: each instrument is a specific color, and composition means arranging colors. His Principles of Orchestration remains the definitive manual of Late Romantic orchestra

items.name: The Rimsky-Korsakov scale (octatonic) as exotic color
items.description: Rimsky-Korsakov regularly used the octatonic scale (alternating whole-step and half-step: C-D-Eb-F-Gb-Ab-A-B-C) for fantasy and supernatural passages. Scheherazade's demonic characters, the magic sect

items.name: Arabian Nights exotic color — modal scales and augmented 2nds
items.description: Scheherazade, the Spanish Capriccio, Antar — Rimsky's exotic subjects call for specific scale types: harmonic minor (with its augmented 2nd between the 6th and 7th degrees), Phrygian mode, Arabic doub

items.name: Brilliant solo woodwind writing — the storyteller's voice
items.description: Rimsky's orchestral solos are legendary: the bassoon in the opening of Scheherazade, the clarinet in the Spanish Capriccio, the flute in Sadko. Each solo is individually crafted for the specific timbr

items.name: Narrative orchestration — music as visual image
items.description: Rimsky's program music is specifically visual: the sea (Scheherazade), the sunrise, the flight of the bumblebee. The orchestration creates these images through specific technical means: string tremolo
